more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; jam, jellies and marmalades and sweetened chestnut purée as defined by Directive 2001/113/EC; batters.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.overview: Dimethylpolysiloxane is a mixture of linear silicone polymers with methyl groups and defined end groups, used to control foaming. Its anti-caking role is to reduce the tendency of particles in a food powder to stick together. The specified material is supplied as colourless liquid. EU permissions include flavoured drinks, fats and oils essentially free from water  (excluding anhydrous milk fat), canned or bottled fruit and vegetables, jam jellies and marmalades and similar products.
